module_title: Panchayati Raj - PESA Act, Exempted Areas, and Compulsory vs. Voluntary Provisions
introduction: This advanced level analyzes the nuances of the 73rd Amendment by splitting its provisions into compulsory and voluntary categories. It also explores the PESA Act designed specifically for tribal areas and the major criticisms regarding the financial autonomy of PRIs.

core_concepts.title: Compulsory vs. Voluntary Provisions
core_concepts.description: Compulsory (Must be implemented by states): 3-tier system, 5-year term, establishing SEC and SFC, reservation for women and SC/STs. Voluntary (State's discretion): Giving reservation to OBCs, granting financial powers to levy taxes, giving representation to MPs/MLAs in panchayats.

core_concepts.title: PESA Act, 1996
core_concepts.description: PESA (Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act was enacted on the recommendation of the Bhuria Committee. It extends the provisions of Part IX to the 5th Schedule areas (tribal areas) with certain modifications to protect the traditional customs, rights, and culture of the tribal population.

core_concepts.title: Powers of Gram Sabha under PESA
core_concepts.description: PESA makes the Gram Sabha extremely powerful. It is endowed with the power to safeguard cultural identity, control over minor forest produce, power to prevent land alienation, and consultation before land acquisition for development projects.

core_concepts.title: Financial Dependency and Criticism
core_concepts.description: The biggest structural weakness of PRIs is their lack of independent financial resources. They rely heavily on tied and untied grants from the Central and State governments because State Legislatures are reluctant to devolve significant taxation powers (voluntary provision) to them.

important_entities.name: Dileep Singh Bhuria
important_entities.significance: His committee's report laid the groundwork for the historic PESA Act of 1996, aiming to align modern democratic decentralization with traditional tribal governance.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment does NOT apply to the states of Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Mizoram, nor does it apply to the 6th Schedule areas (AMTM) and the hill areas of Manipur and Darjeeling. These areas have their own Autonomous District Councils.

Students often assume OBC reservation is constitutionally mandated. It is NOT. Under the 73rd Amendment, providing reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) is entirely a 'Voluntary Provision' left to the state legislature.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram. The 73rd Amendment is not applicable to the tribal areas of these states.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC frequently asks to identify which provisions are 'Compulsory' and which are 'Voluntary'. Create a mental checklist (e.g., Taxes, OBCs, and MP/MLA presence = Voluntary).
In Assertion-Reasoning questions, deeply understand how the PESA Act specifically empowers the 'Gram Sabha' over the higher tiers of the Panchayat in tribal areas.
